The present application has been filed seeking regular bail in connection with FIR No.0432/2022 under Sections 498A/304B/34 IPC registered at Police Station Narela.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the testimony of the mother, as well as, the brother of the deceased has already been recorded.

She submits that the mother of the deceased,
who was examined as PW-1, in her testimony has stated that on three occasions demand of dowry was made by the family of the petitioner.

A demand of Rs.7 lakhs was made initially, whereas, a demand of Rs.10,000/- was made two days before the death of the deceased and the third demand of Rs.1 lakh was made two months prior to the death of the deceased.

3. She submits that insofar as the demand of Rs.7 lakhs is concerned, the same is attributed to the mother of the petitioner and is general in nature, in as much as, no specific date or time has been mentioned.
Insofar as demand of Rs.10,000/- made by the petitioner two days before the death of the deceased is concerned, she submits that there are multiple improvements in the statement of the PW-1.
She invites the attention of the Court to the testimony This is a digitally signed order.

4. As far as the demand of Rs.1 lakh is concerned, she submits that the same does not find mention in the first two statements of the mother of the deceased recorded under Section 161 CrPC.
The said demand has figured only in the third statement of deceased recorded under Section 161 CrPC, which was recorded on 31.08.2022, i.e., ten days after the death of the deceased.
5. She submits that in view of the material contradictions and improvements made by the mother of the deceased, the version of the prosecution has been rendered doubtful.

She submits that the petitioner is in custody since 21.08.2022 and since the investigation is complete and the trial is Deepak Kumar vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177682386/

sentences.text: She further submits that since material witnesses have already been examined, there is no possibility of such witnesses being influenced by the petitioner in the event, the petitioner is enlarged on bail.
7. In view of the above, it is urged by the learned counsel that the petitioner be enlarged on bail.
8. Per contra, learned APP for the State has argued on the lines of the status report.

He submits that the petitioner is residing in a rented accommodation and that there is a possibility that he may flee from justice in case he is enlarged on bail.
9.
I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, as well as, the learned APP for the State and have perused the material on record.
10. Prima facie, there appears to be substance in the submission of the This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:22:48 learned counsel for the petitioner that the mother of the deceased, who was examined as PW-1, has made material improvements in her version.
11. It is clear from the testimony of PW-1 that she was confronted with the statement recorded by the SDM where the demand made with regard to Rs.10,000/- is not mentioned.
Similarly, the allegation of demand of Rs.7 lakhs is general in nature as no time and date of such demand has been stated.

Insofar as demand of Rs.1 lakh is concerned, the same has been mentioned only in the third statement of the PW-1 recorded under Section 161 CrPC that too after a period of ten days from the death of the deceased.

12. Though the probative and evidentiary value of the testimony of PW-1 cannot be gone into at this stage and the same will be appreciated by the learned Trial Court at the appropriate stage but it cannot be outrightly negated that the evidence which has come on record has the potential of making a dent into the case of the prosecution to an extent.

13. Further, the petitioner is in judicial custody since 21.08.2022 and his custody is no more required for any purpose as trial is underway.
14.
Further, perusal of the charge-sheet shows that the prosecution has cited as many as 22 witnesses, of which only 2 have been examined.
Evidently, the trial is not likely to be concluded any time soon.
15. It is not the case of the prosecution that the petitioner is a flight risk.
Further, the antecedents of the petitioner are also clean.

17. Considering the circumstances in entirety, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.
Accordingly, the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:22:48 petitioner is admitted to bail subject to his furnishing a Personal Bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-
and one Surety Bond of the like amount subject to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/Jail Superintendent/Duty Magistrate, further subject to the following conditions:-
a) Petitioner will not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.
b) Petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.

c) Petitioner shall provide his latest/ permanent address, as well as, mobile number to the IO concerned which shall be kept in working condition and he shall not change the mobile number without prior intimation to the Investigating Officer concerned.
d) Petitioner shall not indulge in any criminal activity and shall not communicate with or come in contact with the witnesses or any family members of the witnesses.
18. The petition stands disposed of.
19. Copy of the order be forwarded to the concerned Jail Superintendent or information and necessary compliance.
20. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
21. Order dasti under signatures of the Court Master.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J NOVEMBER 10, 2023/MK
